transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2026-08-29
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Rao (LatticeHealth Head of ML), Tom Alvarez (VP Eng), Sasha Kim (SRE), Leo Park (Product)

Summary: Quick monthly health check focused on an unexpected upward shift in token burn, discussing whether to move parts of traffic to dedicated capacity, and planning performance benchmarks and security documentation handoff.

Topics: usage spike, committed vs hosted economics, latency SLOs, batching and KV cache, private VPC considerations, SOC2 & audit logs, pilot success metrics, next steps.

[00:00] Maya Chen: okay everyone thanks for joining, we got about 50 minutes, we want to go over the spike you saw last week and talk next steps around cost mitigation and the pilot.
[00:12] Priya Rao: yeah thanks Maya, quick context — we saw about a 38% increase in token burn week-over-week after the new recommendation flow launched, the latencies stayed fine but our bill jumped which is a problem for finance.
[00:25] Tom Alvarez: and to add, the spike aligns with higher sequence lengths in multi-turn sessions, we've been seeing more long-form summarization calls.
[00:34] Ethan Patel: okay so that immediately suggests batching and KV cache tuning might help; also dedicated capacity with a higher quantization profile can drop unit cost.
[00:45] Sasha Kim: can we get into numbers, like what % improvement we might expect? finance needs a projection.
[00:51] Ethan Patel: rough thumb — for long sequences, prefix caching can reduce tokens by 20–30% depending on reuse, autoscaling efficiencies on dedicated pools plus int8/4 quantization we typically quote 30–45% unit cost savings, but actual depends on model and prompt distribution.
[01:10] Priya Rao: repeat that — 30–45% is for dedicated plus quantization? you mean compared to hosted standard?
[01:16] Ethan Patel: yes, compared to hosted default runtime. Hosted has its benefits for burst but dedicated is where you see predictable per-token economics.
[01:24] Leo Park: we have concerns about rollout complexity; product wants no degradation in answer quality, and Ops is worried about SOC2 artifacts and SSO.
[01:33] Maya Chen: totally — we can gate dedicated rollout behind automated evaluation runs against your prompt sets; if quality regresses we fallback to hosted variant automatically. we'll also share our SOC2 pack; private VPC option keeps logs in your tenancy.
[01:48] Tom Alvarez: fallback sounds good, how does the automatic fallback work? is that hard to configure?
[01:53] Ethan Patel: it's policy-driven — you can set thresholds on latency, error rate, and quality metrics (we ingest eval scores tied to prompt sets). if a canary underperforms, traffic routes back to a compatible variant. configuration is via the console or YAML.
[02:06] Sasha Kim: console or YAML is fine, but we need audit logs sent to our SIEM and retention options for 2 years for compliance.
[02:13] Maya Chen: we can push logs to your S3 or to a syslog endpoint; retention is configurable in Private and Dedicated. i'll attach the audit-log guide.
[02:22] Priya Rao: one question — our prompts include PHI in some contexts, is that okay on hosted?
[02:28] Maya Chen: for PHI workloads we recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) so you control governance and KMS; Dedicated also supports customer-managed KMS in some configurations.
[02:38] Priya Rao: okay we need the security packet then.
[02:41] Maya Chen: yes will send SOC2 + pen test + KMS docs.
[02:45] Leo Park: back to economics — can we model committed capacity vs variable usage? we have a finance lead who wants a model to decide commitment level.
[02:53] Ethan Patel: we typically provide a 12-month projection spreadsheet: scenario A no commit, scenario B 6mo commit, scenario C 12mo commit with burst. i'll produce that with sample traffic and a conservative savings estimate.
[03:05] Tom Alvarez: perfect, also include a sensitivity column for sequence length variance.
[03:09] Ethan Patel: will do.
[03:11] [03:11] Maya Chen: okay next operational item — the benchmark. Sasha, can Redwood run a week-long throughput test that mirrors your peak load?
[03:19] Sasha Kim: yes we'd need a test plan and access controls. critical to include long tail requests that go 8k tokens.
[03:26] Ethan Patel: that's the plan for the perf run — we'll include 8k token scenarios; can we get your top-50 prompt patterns and traffic shape?
[03:33] Sasha Kim: i'll share that. note we also have a nightly batch job that spikes at 2am UTC — please include that pattern.
[03:40] Ethan Patel: noted. we'll instrument traces so we can show hot spots — kernel backpressure, KV cache miss rates, etc.
[03:47] Priya Rao: another ask — can we get a breakdown of per-route latency and token cost, so product can prioritize routes to shift to dedicated?
[03:55] Maya Chen: yes, Redwood Console has per-route cost and latency views; i'll share permissions and a short guide on how to filter down to routes and tokens.
[04:03] Leo Park: if we move only high-token routes to dedicated, can we keep QA and staging on hosted?
[04:08] Ethan Patel: absolutely, you can split by route and environment. many customers keep dev on hosted and prod on dedicated.
[04:13] [04:13] Tom Alvarez: in terms of SLA — what do we get with Dedicated?
[04:16] Maya Chen: Dedicated comes with an SLA for uptime and a latency target depending on the committed tier; i'll paste the SLA table.
[04:23] Sasha Kim: do you offer a canary rollback policy by default? we want safe rollouts.
[04:28] Ethan Patel: yes, canaries are first-class. you can set percent traffic ramps, evaluation windows, and automated rollback triggers based on error/quality signals.
[04:36] Priya Rao: on the quality signals — we want to run regression checks against our golden prompts every deploy. how are regressions surfaced?
[04:44] Ethan Patel: we surface a regression score and diffed examples in the Console; you can subscribe to alerts and channel them to Slack or email.
[04:51] Maya Chen: quick note — we've already put a subset of your prompt set into the eval pipeline and will attach the initial report after this call.
[04:58] Leo Park: nice. any blockers from our side to start a pilot?
[05:02] Priya Rao: we need the security docs, committed pricing, and the perf test plan. also an internal signoff timeline — we'll aim to decide by 2026-09-15.
[05:13] Maya Chen: good target. we'll send pricing by EOD Monday and propose bench windows for the week of Sept 6.
[05:20] Sasha Kim: about the perf run, do you simulate KV cache cold-starts? that's where we've seen worst latency.
[05:27] Ethan Patel: yes we'll include cold-start scenarios and cache warm-up curves, and show token cost impact.
[05:33] Tom Alvarez: about tooling — will you share a runbook for failover from Dedicated back to Hosted? Ops needs a playbook.
[05:40] Maya Chen: yes, runbook and an example rollback YAML. i'll include contact escalation matrix for on-call.
[05:46] Priya Rao: any mention of competitor approaches — i know our infra team looked at Anthropic's dedicated offering. are there big differences?
[05:53] Ethan Patel: conceptually similar but we differentiate on prefix caching and KV cache instrumentation, plus the transparent per-route cost breakdown and our fallback routing features.
[06:03] Leo Park: price/perf comparisons would help; please include comparable benchmarks if you have them.
[06:08] Ethan Patel: i'll include a short appendix with public benchmark references and a tailored comparison.
[06:13] [06:13] Maya Chen: okay let's run through action items so we leave with alignment.
[06:17] Maya Chen: Ethan to run 72-hour perf test (8k sequences), instrument KV misses, and return results; due 2026-09-03.
[06:24] Ethan Patel: noted.
[06:25] Maya Chen: Maya to send committed pricing and 12-month projection by 2026-08-31.
[06:30] Maya Chen: Sasha to share traffic shape & top-50 prompts by 2026-09-02.
[06:35] Sasha Kim: yes.
[06:36] Maya Chen: Priya to confirm pilot success criteria and SLA tolerance by 2026-09-07.
[06:41] Priya Rao: will do.
[06:43] Maya Chen: i'll also attach the SOC2 + pen test and KMS integration docs right after this call (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/latticehealth-packet).
[06:55] Tom Alvarez: thanks, one last item — can we have a 30-minute deep-dive after you deliver the perf results to walk through the graphs?
[07:03] Maya Chen: yes we'll schedule a results playback with SE and SRE present.
[07:08] Priya Rao: great, thanks everyone.
[07:10] [07:10] Meeting ended

Notes about transcription: speaker labels are best-effort; some overlapping talk and filler words were transcribed. References shared: pricing spreadsheet (link: https://redwood.example.com/pricing/latticehealth-projection.xlsx), perf test plan (link: https://redwood.example.com/tests/latticehealth-perf-plan.md), security packet (link: https://redwood.example.com/security/latticehealth-packet), regression watchlist (Console alert).
